summary.headline: IFB Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16.65% to INR 1,529 crores, with PAT up to INR 38.06 crores, but commodity and forex costs were not passed on to customers.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.65% YoY to INR 1,529 crores and PBDIT rose 26.46% to INR 88.46 crores, with margin up to 5.79% from 5.34%. PAT reached INR 38.06 crores (2.5% of revenue) versus INR 25.36 crores a year earlier. Management said commodity and forex headwinds are not behind the company and have not been passed on to customers, though some price increases were taken. Home Appliances (HAD) volume and revenue growth of about 18% was the main driver, offset by a 160 bps fall in gross margin from material costs. Engineering met its budget with 17% sales growth, while the Steel division posted a loss.

financial_highlights.change: FY26 full year: about INR 67 crores
Above budget; EBITDA in line with budget

segments.name: Home Appliances (HAD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 18% in Q1, with growth in all lines. Front-load volume grew about 9-10%, top-load over 20%, and AC 6-8%. July was described as good. Management stated HAD PBT was about 4.5% of revenue versus about 4% last year.

segments.name: Room AC
segments.commentary: Growth lagged the industry (about 20%+ per analyst). Old-rated stock was run down by January and the new BEE rating is about 10-15% costlier than the market. Capacity is about 75,000 units/month, peak utilisation about 85%, with a target of 75,000-80,000 via debottlenecking.

segments.name: Engineering
segments.commentary: Sales up 17% YoY, above budget, with EBITDA in line with budget. Management targets about INR 2,000 crores revenue, with current run-rate about INR 1,000-1,100 crores. Stamping capex is about INR 400 crores; a Tata battery-project LOI of about INR 150 crores is under review after Tata Sons' reported decision.

segments.name: Steel
segments.commentary: Loss-making in Q1 because steel prices rose about INR 4,125/MT in the quarter. Management expects recovery from customers in coming quarters; ROCE is targeted around 20%.

segments.name: Services (HAD)
segments.commentary: Services revenue growth of about 17% YoY in Q1 as stated; management described services profitability as double-digit at PBT level.

segments.name: IFB Refrigeration (associate, 41.40% stake)
segments.commentary: Associate PBT about INR 80 lakhs in Q1; IFB's share about INR 0.33 crores. Management declined to discuss the company's performance. Its refrigerator sales are 2% growth versus 14% for IFB branches.

guidance_outlook: HAD growth of about 20% targeted; management said Q1's 18% is the path, and that growth should continue in coming quarters.
Cost initiatives of INR 120-150 crores targeted for FY27, with INR 42-43 crores already achieved in Q1.
Management said commodity and forex pressure is not yet behind the company and hopes it eases over time.
Long-term HAD PBDIT aspiration is early double digits; AC market-share aspiration is 7-10% without a timeline.
Capex for the full year is about INR 110 crores (Engineering commentary); Engineering plans about INR 1,000 crores business with about INR 400 crores Stamping capex, contingent on OEM orders.
Management expects Engineering to deliver a similar growth rate to Q1 for the year.
capex_capacity: Room AC capacity about 75,000 units/month, with peak-month utilisation about 85%; debottlenecking and automation planned to reach 75,000-80,000 without added shifts.
Management said there is no capacity constraint in HAD; capacity can be increased through debottlenecking without major investment.
Engineering: land acquired in Gujarat for EV and stamping; stamping capacity expansion planned in Gujarat, Gurgaon and Bangalore.
Battery (Tata LOI, about INR 150 crores) on hold pending Tata Agratas' decision; machinery not yet bought.
Over the next 3-6 months, HAD expects to add products for capacities it does not currently serve.
demand_pricing: Commodity and forex costs were not passed to customers in the form of price increases, since management wants to stay competitively priced.
Price increases were taken across all categories in the last quarter, but these were not enough to cover commodity and forex; some were taken even where the market had not followed.
Front-loader SKUs cut from about 55-57 models to 24-25; washer SKUs roughly halved from about 9,500.
Management said it is in the top 2 in front-load, and possibly top 4 or lower in top-load, but no published share data exists.
Trade schemes and discounts were about INR 1,800 crores (per analyst question); management said this is an industry practice and under review for leakages.
Gross margin fell about 160 bps, offset by lower opex as a % of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Has the commodity and forex increase been passed on, and is it behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, the pressure is ongoing and not behind the company. Price increases were not enough to pass the full commodity/forex cost to the market; cost efficiencies offset part of it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did RAC growth (about 10%) lag the industry (about 20%+)?
qa_highlights.answer: The company deliberately ran out old-rated AC stock by January rather than carry it forward. The new BEE-rated models are about 10-15% costlier than the market, so the price advantage was lost. Focus is shifting to higher-capacity models.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Services business's growth and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Services grew about 17% YoY in Q1. It includes refrigerator services at 100% on approval basis. Management said profitability is double-digit at PBT level.

qa_highlights.question: Will cost savings be maintained as SKUs are rationalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost initiatives are INR 42-43 crores in Q1 and INR 120-150 crores targeted for FY27, with no cut to counters or in-store promoters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Steel division loss and the plan to fix it?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel loss is due to a steel price increase of about INR 4,125/MT in Q1, which management expects to recover from customers in the coming quarters. ROCE is about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the front-load, top-load and AC volume growth rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Front-load grew about 9-10%, top-load over 20%, and AC 6-8%, per management.

risks_watch: Commodity and forex pressure is ongoing with no price pass-through; gross margin fell about 160 bps.
Competitive pricing constraints: management said it does not want to be disadvantaged, and the price-increase ability depends on peers.
RAC growth lag and the new BEE rating (10-15% costlier than the market); the 7-10% market-share aspiration has no timeline.
Engineering's INR 2,000 crore target depends on the Tata battery project and new OEM businesses; LOI about INR 150 crores is on hold.
Steel division loss, with price recovery expected in coming quarters.
Data inconsistencies: the Fine Blanking Q1 FY26 revenue figure differs between presentations (INR 185-186 crores vs INR 176 crores); the Motor division loss is pending an offline response.
IFB Refrigeration (associate) growth gap: 14% for IFB branches versus 2% company-wide; management declined to discuss it.
High trade schemes and discounts (about INR 1,800 crores per analyst) are under review.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and top-line momentum (18% HAD growth, 20% target), but cautious and defensive on margins, commodity and forex, and pricing. Management evaded or deferred several questions (associate refrigeration performance, Motor division, Fine Blanking base, Tata battery project).
key_quotes: And whether it is behind us, as of now, no. So we are still seeing commodity increases that are there, as well as Forex.
We have not been able to pass on the commodity and Forex to the customer in the form of a price increase.
So we are not diluting our product. We continue to maintain the high standards that IFB is well known for.
We are definitely on track as far as the INR150 crores cost initiatives are concerned.

adds.what: Room AC capacity debottlenecking to 75,000-80,000 units/month (from ~75,000 units/month) without added shifts
Engineering stamping capacity expansion in Gujarat, Gurgaon and Bangalore (about INR 400 crore stamping capex, contingent on OEM orders)

growth.why: Management targets about 20% HAD revenue growth for FY27 (Q1 at 18%), backed by price increases, demand gains and new products, with cost initiatives of INR 120-150 crore; no firm capacity or order numbers were given for the 20% target, and Room AC debottlenecking and Engineering stamping capex (INR 400 crore, contingent on OEM orders) are not yet firm.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin fell about 160 bps on material costs, commodity and forex pressure is ongoing with no pass-through, and PBDIT margin only reached 5.79% (from 5.34%) largely on opex cuts and cost initiatives of INR 42-43 crore in Q1.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Room AC debottlenecking to 75,000-80,000 units/month (about 6.7% uplift from 75,000) is planned without added shifts, and Engineering stamping capex of about INR 400 crore is planned in Gujarat, Gurgaon and Bangalore but contingent on OEM orders; no firm dates were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: HAD revenue grew about 18% in Q1 with front-load volume up 9-10%, top-load over 20% and AC 6-8%; management says 20% growth is the target and July was good, though AC lagged the industry.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Room AC peak utilisation is about 85%, which is high, but management said there is no HAD capacity constraint and plans debottlenecking rather than new plants; Engineering stamping capex (about INR 400 crore) is contingent on OEM orders and the Tata battery LOI (about INR 150 crore) is on hold.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is holding the 20% HAD growth target against Q1's 18%, is not passing on commodity and forex costs, and expects Engineering growth similar to Q1's 17%, so there is no clear basis for a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Commodity and forex pressure is ongoing, gross margin fell about 160 bps, Steel posted a loss on a INR 4,125/MT steel price rise, and the Tata battery LOI (about INR 150 crore) is on hold, so the INR 2,000 crore Engineering target and 20% HAD growth carry execution risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management said HAD expects to add products for capacities it does not currently serve over the next 3-6 months, and the new BEE-rated RAC models are being shifted to, though no specific products were named.

rows.label: FY27 cost initiatives of INR 120-150 crore
rows.why: INR 42-43 crore already achieved in Q1 against INR 67 crore for all of FY26, so the INR 120-150 crore full-year target needs about INR 78-108 crore more over the remaining three quarters.

rows.label: Pass-through of commodity and forex costs
rows.why: Management said commodity and forex costs were not passed on, price increases were not enough to cover them, and it wants to stay competitively priced, so pricing power is limited.

rows.label: Engineering OEM and Tata battery orders
rows.why: The INR 2,000 crore Engineering target against a current run-rate of about INR 1,000-1,100 crore depends on new OEM business and the Tata battery LOI (about INR 150 crore), which is on hold pending Tata Agratas' decision.
